chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Al-Yamani and as-Sufyani are like two racehorses.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: As-Sufyani, a tyrannical figure who rises before the Mahdi, known for his oppression and bloodshed.
key_terms.الْيَمَانِيُّ: Al-Yamani, a key figure who rises before the Mahdi, known for his sincerity and guidance.
key_terms.فَرَسَي رَهَانَ: Two racehorses, a metaphor indicating speed, prominence, and distinct identity in their respective roles.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the comparison between Al-Yamani and As-Sufyani to racehorses in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) likens Al-Yamani and As-Sufyani to 'two racehorses' (kafarsayi rahin), a metaphor emphasizing their rapid, simultaneous emergence and intense rivalry in the end times. In Shia eschatology, this comparison highlights that while both are major signs, their trajectories and impacts will be distinct yet parallel, serving as pivotal events preceding the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him).

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (15) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa from Ibraheem bin Hashim from Muhammad bin Abu Omayr from Hisham bin Salim that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “
Al-Yamani and as-Sufyani will rise like two racehorses.”
